fields.description: Issue focuses on Miami municipal politics ahead of the Nov. 15, 1949 primary, including discussion of the Greater Miami Crime Commission’s role in endorsing or influencing city commission candidates and a published telephone poll listing leading candidates. Coverage includes criticism of Florida’s new sales tax and Dade County assessments and zoning disputes (including West Shores/Miami Shores area), a report on a candidate repudiating an alleged Communist Party leaflet, and commentary on public-utility telephone practices. The issue also contains reporting on an alleged baby-placement/adoption racket and references to a Miami physician, and an international political piece on Cuban figure Jose Manuel Aleman and a proposed U.S.–Cuban loan, along with local columns and advertisements.
